title: Three kinds of leader
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Which kind of leader are you now, and which do you want to be?

A student summarized chapter 3: there are different types of leaders. One works behind the scenes, is really good at the job and does not talk about their authority. One is ego driven: look at me, look how much money I made. The third is the mission-driven leader, whom the book calls the best for today's business culture.

Jose said that he likes the mission-driven leader and the servant leader, and that he works with his sons so they do not buy into social-media entrepreneurs who push I am this and I am that and you can do the same.

Jose said that he comes from a military background, which is a very top-down style: this is what you are going to do, just do it. He said it is ego driven, and that in a conflict you cannot stop and discuss.

He said that this style is still used in corporations, and it can be effective in certain circumstances. He said the book describes a different style of leading, and that self-knowledge is one of the characteristics: how to make people aware that through self-knowledge they empower themselves.
A student said: the best-kept-secret leader resonated with me; I could see how I am that person, and I want to be more of the mission-driven, thought leader.
Which of the three do your people see?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write which of the three kinds you are most days.
Write what a mission-driven version of you would do differently.
Write one self-knowledge question you will ask each week.

check.q: Which leader does the book say is best for today, according to a student?
What did Jose say about the top-down style?
choices: It can be effective in certain circumstances

check.q: What did Jose say is one of the characteristics of the new style?

recap: Know the three kinds of leader. Aim for mission and service.
